Selected work

Research projects

These projects reflect my development from reproducing established dynamical models to designing independent computational studies. For each project, I describe the question, what I contributed, and the limits of the evidence.

CONCEPTUAL VIEWCONTINUOUS MEMORY MANIFOLD
Independent research · 2025—presentSignature Work Distinction

Sleep Replay on Continuous Memory Manifolds

I asked whether replay timing and neural overlap could determine whether similar memories blend together or become easier to distinguish.

I developed a label-free computational model and a matched 4,032-row simulation study. In a bounded parameter regime, replay separated previously confused memories by 0.0517 radians and reduced recall error by 0.00710 radians. I then ran a locked replication across 48 simulated subjects, built an excitatory/inhibitory implementation, and tested recovery under sparse and noisy conditions.

Continuous attractors · neural fields · circular statistics · bootstrap and permutation inference · MATLAB · Python

SE(2) CONSISTENCY0.8568 LOCKED MACRO AUROC
Independent collaborator · 2026Manuscript submitted

Geometry-Informed SE(2) Consistency Monitoring

We asked whether consistency across coordinate-frame transformations could provide an interpretable signal for online robotic fault monitoring.

I developed a lightweight neural controller and a detector combining equivariance residuals, kinematic deviations, and command–observation mismatches. The detector was calibrated on healthy trajectories and evaluated across eight simulated fault types, including locked and out-of-distribution tests. It achieved 0.8568 macro AUROC on the untouched locked q50 partition.

SE(2) equivariance · anomaly detection · robotic control · locked validation · PyTorch · Python

Jianfeng Lu Lab · Duke UniversityResearch assistant · 2024

Attractor Networks, Forgetting, and Chaos

This project examined how network regimes shape transitions among stable recall, drift, and memory loss.

I developed and tuned attractor-network models, applied dynamical mean-field theory, and reproduced results from Physical Review X 13, 011009 across more than 300 MATLAB simulations. I also documented the implementation so that later researchers could reuse and extend it.

Attractor networks · dynamical mean-field theory · nonlinear dynamics · MATLAB · reproducibility
